item.title: Kimi Antonelli Lost the São Paulo GP Lead to a Spin He Still Can’t Explain
item.description: Kimi Antonelli says he’s “very angry” after a spin he can’t explain cost him the lead and a likely win in the F1 São Paulo GP. It was a solid start from Mercedes’ Antonelli when he took the lead from McLaren’s Lando Norris in the F1 São Paulo GP. He held on well while Norris fought Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson and defended from Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar. The 2026 F1 champion had the lead under control, but he started to complain about problems that Mercedes teammate George Russell felt too. Antonelli struggled to stop the car and lost the rear at Turn 1. That cost him places, and the problem lasted the rest of the Grand Prix. He finished fifth, behind Norris, the Red Bull pair and Russell. Kimi Antonelli and George Russell battle in the F1 São Paulo GP. Image Credit: Michael Potts/LAT Images Antonelli Says the Spin Came With “No Warning” “I’m very disappointed with the race,” Antonelli told the media. “I’m very angry, to be fair. [It was] very disappointing, because we were on for the win up to that point. Also, on the slick, once I was able to get some temperature, I got into the rhythm. “But the spin came, which is still something I need to look at, because I don’t know why I lost the rear so quickly as well. Like, no warning, nothing. But already, to be fair, when I put the soft on, I felt something weird with the car. “So, we need to check what happened. But on the other hand, a shame, because we lost the race there,” said Antonelli, who really wanted to win the Grand Prix in Brazil, especially after visiting Ayrton Senna’s museum. Mercedes Still Clinched the Constructors’ Title Mercedes celebrates its 2026 F1 constructors’ title at Interlagos. Image Credit: Jiri Krenek/Active Pictures “I really wanted to win here in Brazil, in front of this amazing crowd,” continued Antonelli. “The support has been so special this weekend, and it would have been good to finish with a win. It’s a shame that I missed out. Hopefully, next year we’ll come back stronger, and we’re going to be able to win it.” Mercedes still had reason to celebrate, even with fourth and fifth. The team clinched the 2026 F1 constructors’ title , its first since 2021, and Antonelli joined the celebrations on the podium. “I’m going to put all this aside for now, because we clinched the title for the team, and they all deserve it,” said Antonelli. “And I’m very proud to be part of this group and this team, who have done and still do so much for me, and I’m very happy for them.”

item.title: Bruins’ Morgan Geekie Finding Scoring Touch Again
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins have gotten their leading goal scorer from last season back on the scoresheet, and he’s caught some fire. After starting the season with one goal in the first 14 games, Morgan Geekie has goals in each of the last four games. He is now tied for third on the Bruins’ roster with five goals this season, and his three power-play goals are tied for the team lead. Geekie shrugged the slump off as it was happening; it’s easy to do that when the Bruins are at the top of the Atlantic Division. He also mentioned prioritizing quality shots, which helps to explain the 21.8% shooting percentage and 72 goals over the last two seasons. “I’ve always thought that a quality shot is better than a quantity shot. And I think that’s maybe in some cases the wrong mentality, but just kind of how I’ve always played,” Geekie said in late October. “But it’s one of those things where, you know, maybe you have to change your mentality a little bit when you don’t see pucks go in.” Read Next Bruins’ Morgan Geekie Looks to Regain Scoring Touch Geekie started the season with one goal on 17 shots, or a shooting percentage of 5.9%. He also carried an average of 1.21 shots per game. Since then, he’s scored four goals on 12 shots, a 33.3% shooting percentage, while averaging three shots per game. “Just opportunity,” Geekie said on Monday when asked about increasing his shot volume. “I think I was passing up a few to begin with. I also think, lately, I’ve been finding myself kind of on that left side where I like to be, and I’ve had a few shots on the power play. Especially (Sunday). Just try to find those little spots that I think you maybe get away from when you’re not getting shots, and try to get back to them. My game doesn’t change a whole lot when things aren’t going in, but when they are, I feel like you find yourself in those spots a little bit more than normal.” The opportunities are coming on the power play. Geekie averaged 2.5 shot attempts per game at 5-on-5 over his first 14 games, and that number has not changed over the last four. His shot attempts in all situations, however, have jumped from 3.57 to 5.5 per game, according to Natural Stat Trick . He has a selective approach to his shots, but when they start to fall, the confidence comes back. “Not much changes. I think when you have that confidence to kind of shoot the puck, I think you see yourself taking a few more opportunities to do so and being less afraid to do it,” Geekie said. “It doesn’t really change how I’m playing or anything like that, but I think when you find yourself in spots where maybe you wouldn’t shoot before, you have the confidence to shoot it just because you’ve seen it go in the last few games.” Geekie has also been dangerous from the left circle, where he has found success on the power play. He was so excited and then he didn't. And so he called NASCAR and he was like, 'I want to see the numbers. How far off was I? Was I close?' Kyle was very competitive, and he took this no differently." Later that night, Samantha took the stage to accept the award for Kyle, who died on May 21st of this year at just 41 years old. item.title: Chelsea frustrated by Hacken in women's Champions League, Man City win
item.description: Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk frustrated Chelsea (Adam Ihse/TT) Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition. The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay. Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand. However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal -- both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor's side -- could leapfrog them this matchday. "It's a frustrating result," Blues boss Bompastor told UEFA. "We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn't go that way. We need to learn from this." Women's Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings. A first-half Aoba Fujino brace cancelled out Elisa Bartoli's opener for the hosts by half-time. Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table. Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference. Klara Buehl's strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek's early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position. Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on. PSG lie in ninth place on five points. In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes. A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada's side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points. Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after. Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder's reverse pass. "It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn't won any of our first three games," Caruso said. "We have to try to finish among the top teams." item.title: Zé Lucas rallies fans for Belém U20 games: “Our home, this is Brazil”
item.description: Zé Lucas rallies fans for Belém U20 games: “Our home, this is Brazil” Brazil’s Under-20 national team continued preparations on Tuesday (10) for their friendlies against Peru at the Mangueirão in Belém. Tuesday (10) marked the first training session in which coach Paulo Victor had the full squad at his disposal. One of the team’s key players, defensive midfielder Zé Lucas spoke about adapting to the climate and the stadium, and revealed that, as the first match approaches, the players are starting to feel the benefits of home advantage: “This is our home, this is Brazil.” A good performance starts with settling in well. Defensive midfielder Zé Lucas said Brazil’s Under-20 team are excited about Belém, “a new city unlocked” for most of the players. “We’re adapting to the city too, a new city for us as Brazil players. It’s a new city unlocked,” he said. Zé Lucas during a ball drill at the Mangueirão as Brazil’s Under-20 team prepare for their friendlies against Peru Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF Known for its passion for football, the capital of Pará has the players excited about the prospect of fan support. The midfielder spoke about the squad’s anticipation of playing in front of the crowd, called on fans to come out and promised a committed performance to put on a good show. “Our expectations couldn’t be higher, because this is our home, this is Brazil. So I believe the fans will turn out in numbers and support us, as they’ve always supported Brazil. Regardless of the age group, if it’s the Brazilian national team, the fans are there. So we’re really looking forward to that, and we hope we can repay all their support on the pitch with plenty of effort, fight and determination, wearing a shirt that carries so much history,” he said. A South American Under-17 champion in 2025, Zé Lucas aims to repeat the achievement with the Under-20 team in 2027 Credits: Joilson Marconne / CBF Zé Lucas speaks from experience when he mentions the unwavering support across all age groups. In 2025, he won the South American title with Brazil’s Under-17 team under coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci. Now working with Paulo Victor in Brazil’s yellow shirt, he hopes to repeat that success by winning the Under-20 competition. “Last year, Patetuci gave me a lot of confidence. Coach Paulo Victor is also giving us a lot of confidence here, not just me, but the whole squad. The group feels relaxed and ready to do what he asks and deliver in the best way possible,” he said. Tuesday’s session focused on refining the team’s playing style, with drills involving movement, passing, crossing and finishing. Training also included work on attacking and defensive organisation. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Tigers' Scott Harris lays out top priority as free agency gets moving
item.description: LAS VEGAS — In Sin City, Tigers president Scott Harris seems eager to double-down. One year after the Tigers stocked up on pitching in the hot-stove season, they appear to be preparing to let it ride on arms again. Pitching remains the Tigers' priority this offseason, Harris said Tuesday, Nov. 10, on the first day of the general managers meetings at Aria on the Strip. Specifically, Harris singled out relief pitching. And beyond that, he highlighted swing-and-miss relief pitching. The Tigers' bullpen was bottom 10 in Major League Baseball in strikeouts in 2026. The Tigers' bullpen blew exactly half of their save opportunities — 32 of 64 — which was a prime culprit behind them finishing the season 76-86, and missing the postseason for the first time since 2023. "We want to add more swing-and-miss in the back end of our pen. We want to add like a stable veteran presence who can get righties out and get lefties out and add a little more leadership to our clubhouse," Harris said Tuesday in a conversation with reporters that lasted nearly a full hour. "If we can find that, that'd be great." That pitcher (or pitchers) doesn't necessarily have to be a closer, Harris said, in reiterating his long-standing philosophy in working with manager AJ Hinch. More: MLB free-agency has begun: Here are 10 possible targets for the Tigers But it's worth noting that the Tigers don't have a player signed who had more than two saves for them last year. Will Vest (two saves) struggled on the mound and with his health in 2026, undergoing hip and elbow surgeries. "My job is just to fill the roster with really good arms," said Harris, "and let AJ sort it all out." The Tigers this offseason decided to part ways with veteran closer Kenley Jansen, two saves shy of him reaching 500 for his career. They declined his option after an up-and-down season that didn't live up to the expectations when they signed him for $11 million in 2026. He had a 3.20 ERA and 1.044 WHIP, and his strikeouts per nine innings were up from 2025 (10.2, from 8.7). But other numbers were more alarming, especially walks per nine innings (4.6) and FIP (4.46). Home runs per nine innings also were up slightly, and he gave up some huge home runs. The Tigers also re-signed Kyle Finnegan to a two-year, $19-million deal last offseason, and he had a very rough 2026, with a WHIP of 1.665. Finnegan will be back for 2027, and it's likely he'll have some new bullpen mate or three as Harris acknowledged the minor-league pipeline to the back end of the bullpen isn't where the organization wants it. "So we're going to have to find different acquisition avenues to add to our 'pen right now," Harris said. If the Tigers do go shopping for a closer-type reliever, veteran right-handed closers David Bednar, 32, and Raisel Iglesias, 36, are two of the top names on the market. item.title: The southpaw flamethrower
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Adrian Morejon #50 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers during the seventh inning in game one of the National League Division Series at American Family Field on October 03, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Adrian Morejon When the Padres signed Adrian Morejon out of Cuba in 2016, it was a big deal. At the time, the left-hander was ranked second overall among international prospects. The 17-year-old came over and began to pitch quite well as a starting pitcher, posting a sub-4.00 ERA in his first two minor-league seasons. Morejon made his debut in 2019 and struggled to find his footing. His stuff never quite played out as a starter, so San Diego transitioned him into the bullpen. Injuries held him back, with Morejon throwing just 47 2/3 big-league innings from 2021-23. Overall Grade: A- Then, everything changed. In 2024, Morejon became one of the most dominant relief pitchers in baseball. He took it to another level in 2025 and was nearly as good in ‘26. Morejon twirled a career-high 86 innings, posting a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP and .205 opponent batting average. He accumulated 107 strikeouts and 1.9 bWAR in that time. His only problem were blips in April (6.43 ERA) and September (4.50 ERA). His underlying metrics are even better. Morejon’s expected stats (xERA and xBA) are both roughly 50 points lower than his actual marks. His sinker was one of the best in baseball (+11 Pitching Run Value), ranking him fifth among all relievers in PRV. Among all pitchers (starters and relievers) who threw more than 500 sinkers, Morejon ranks sixth overall in PRV. Morejon was issued a $23.15 million qualifying offer last week. He has until Nov. 17 to decide whether he will remain with the Padres another season or decline and test free agency. Morejon is high on San Diego’s wish list out of their departing free agents. Many of the Friar Faithful hope that he’ll remain a Padre for his whole career. Only time will tell if ownership is willing to spend what is required to retain the lefty’s services.

item.title: Celtics lottery pick Aaron Nesmith on the importance of opportunity
item.description: MEXICO CITY - To Aaron Nesmith, opportunity matters. The former Vanderbilt alum has found exactly that with the team the Boston Celtics traded him to, Nesmith having carved out a role on the wing with the Indiana Pacers , his trademark style of physical play and shooting a key part of Indiana's approach to the game. The Celtics Wire caught up with him in Mexico City for the 2026 NBA Mexico City Game, where his Pacers squad fell to Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets . "We're a team that's very dependent on one another for our success, and we've got to have everybody firing in all at all on all cylinders at all times," said Indiana head coach Rick Carlisle of his import to the team after the loss. And while the Pacers may not have come back home with a win for their efforts, Nesmith still saw value in simply making the trip to Mexico. "Even being from the U.S., I didn't get the chance to see NBA players as a kid," said Nesmith. "So for these kids to be able to see us play, it's an honor coming out to their home country." Opportunity (or it's lack) also helped hasten the end of his time with the Celtics, the South Carolina native finding doors open to him in Indiana that were never going to with a stacked roster ahead of him in Boston. "You've got to be able to make mistakes and learn from those mistakes," said Nesmith. "People don't get better by looking over their shoulder. They get better by giving 100 percent." With the Pacers, the opportunity is there, and so far, so has the effort. And with injuries derailing the start of what was supposed to a bounce-back campaign for Indiana, the former Celtic's team will need him to be better than ever. item.title: Takeaways as David Stearns discusses Mets' offseason at GM meetings
item.description: As Major League Baseball's GM meetings got underway in Las Vegas on Tuesday, the congregation of baseball leaders came in front of the backdrop of a looming lockout on Dec. 1. While the club's owners and Major League Baseball Players Association aim to negotiate a new labor agreement that will not lead to spring training or the regular season being interrupted, there is less than a month of runway for front offices to begin to craft a vision for their roster for 2027. For Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns, the plan is to stay the course in the face of uncertainty about the framework within teams might have to operate in the future. "From my perspective, I look at this as a business-as-usual offseason until they tell us otherwise, so we're going through this as though we're going to have a full complete offseason, and I think that's the best way to operate," Stearns told reporters on Tuesday. The first step is approaching the top free agent in this offseason's marketplace. The Mets will meet with two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal next week, according to multiple reports. The New York Post's Jon Heyman was the first to report the meeting. Stearns offered some more clues about the approach that the Mets could take for building their team this offseason. As the GM meetings kicked off, here are three takeaways from what Stearns told the media: How do the Mets plan to address the starting rotation? With a combined 43 wins, 2.42 ERA and 655 strikeouts in the last three seasons, Skubal is the obvious crown jewel available this offseason.
